The meeting was rescheduled to a less inconvenient time.
leave: to go away from a place, or to allow something to remain
She will leave the office early to catch her train.
company: a business organization that makes or sells goods or services
The company announced plans to open three new stores next year.
persuades: convinces someone to do or believe something
A good salesperson persuades customers without making them feel pressured.
regulators: official bodies that control an activity or industry
Financial regulators fined the bank for breaking several trading rules.
adopt: to choose to take up or start using an idea, method, or child
Many schools plan to adopt the new reading program next year.
specification: a detailed description of requirements or standards for something
The engineers followed the client's exact specification for the bridge.
buying: Buying in bulk usually works out cheaper per item.
durable: able to last a long time without breaking
These boots are durable enough to last for many years.
patent: an official right to be the sole maker or seller of an invention
The engineer applied for a patent on her new battery design.
expires: comes to an end; stops being valid
A patent expires, but a habit formed around it does not.
habit: a thing done regularly, almost without thinking
Checking his phone first thing every morning became a habit.
also: The recipe also works well with chicken instead of beef.
intervention: action taken to improve or prevent a situation
Early medical intervention greatly improved the patient's chances of recovery.
works: This explains why rereading notes feels productive and works so poorly.
tends: is likely to do or be something, usually
The market tends to be quieter on rainy weekday mornings.
arrive: to reach a place or come to happen
The train is expected to arrive at the station on time.
early: before the usual or expected time
She always arrives early for important meetings.
before: earlier than a particular time or event
Please arrive at the airport before your flight is due to leave.
grown: having developed or increased over time
The ivy has grown all the way up to the roof this summer.
intervening: becoming involved in a situation, especially to prevent harm
Intervening early in a dispute often prevents it from getting worse.
often: He often walks to work instead of taking the bus.
dismissed: rejected or refused to consider seriously
Her concerns were dismissed by the committee without discussion.
meddling: interfering in something that is not one's concern
He accused his neighbour of meddling in family matters that were not his business.
inconvenience: trouble or difficulty caused to a person's plans or comfort
We apologise for any inconvenience caused by the road closure.
obvious: easy to see or understand; clear
It was obvious from her face that something was wrong.
generate: to produce or bring something into existence
Solar panels generate electricity from sunlight.
political: relating to government, public affairs, or politics
The debate quickly turned into a political argument about taxes.
pressure: a feeling of stress caused by demands or difficulties
The manager felt under pressure to finish the project by Friday.
removing: the act of taking something away
Removing the old wallpaper took most of the weekend.
risen: past participle of rise; increased or moved upward
đã nở lên, đã tăng lên
Prices have risen sharply since the beginning of the year.
match: to be equal to, suitable for, or the same as something else
Her skills perfectly match the requirements of the new job.
none: not any of a group of people or things
None of the students had heard of the composer before.
argues: gives reasons to support an opinion
The report argues for stricter regulation of online advertising.
abolishing: the act of officially ending a law, system, or practice
Abolishing the outdated rule freed the department to work faster.
strange: unusual or surprising; difficult to understand
There was something strange about the silence in the house.
lesson: a period of teaching, or something learned from experience
The teacher planned an interactive lesson about the water cycle.
take: to get hold of, remove, or carry something
Please take a seat while you wait for the doctor.
world: the earth and all its people and things
The trouble starts when the body's clock and the world's clock disagree.
held: supported or kept in a position; past tense of hold
The bridge was held up by a network of steel cables.
point: Mark the point where the two roads meet on the map.
narrower: smaller in width or more limited in scope, comparatively
The new road is narrower than the old highway it replaced.
become: It can take years of practice to become a skilled musician.
invisible: Radio waves are invisible but carry signals across long distances.
nobody: not a single person; no one
Nobody expected the small team to win the championship.
notices: becomes aware of something; sees or observes something
She rarely notices when the room needs cleaning.
everything: all things; the whole of something
Warmth speeds everything up, and dough rises quickly in a hot kitchen.
obeys: does what someone tells them, or follows a rule
The machine obeys a simple set of instructions every time.
thereby: by that means; as a result of that action
She finished early, thereby giving herself time to relax.
adopted: chosen and put into use; taken as one's own
The adopted policy reduced waste across all city offices.
right: correct or suitable for a particular situation
Choosing the right moment to speak up can be difficult.
moment: a very short period of time, or a particular point in time
She paused for a moment before answering the question.
achievements: things successfully accomplished, typically through effort or skill
Her academic achievements earned her a full scholarship abroad.
confusing: gây nhầm lẫn, làm lẫn lộn
The instructions were so confusing that nobody assembled the shelf correctly.
much: to a great extent or degree
The new design does not cost much more than the old one.
think: to use the mind to consider something or form an opinion
I need some time to think before I answer you.
clearly: in a way that is easy to see, hear, or understand
She explained the process clearly so nobody was confused.
set: went down below the horizon, as the sun does
By the time we reached the beach, the sun had already set.
now: at the present time; at this moment
Now is a good time to start saving for retirement.
while: It makes the city liveable while the wider problem is dealt with separately.
cheap: Street food here is cheap and surprisingly delicious.
